# Label

```tsx
import { Label, labelVariants } from "@lucasdost/design-system"
```

The label of a control, with the optional requirement text and Info icon, which shows the `info` text in a tooltip. Mirrors the Figma .Label, .Label Read Only and .Label Disabled components as one component: `state` picks the colors. The Input components already render it from their `label` prop.

## Example

From the Storybook story; names like `args` or `label` are the story controls.

```tsx
<div className="flex w-80 flex-col gap-2">
  <Label {...args} htmlFor="story-label-input" />
  <InputText id="story-label-input" placeholder="Placeholder" />
</div>
```

## Figma notes

Mirrors the Figma .Label, .Label Read Only and .Label Disabled components, which are one component here: `state` picks the colors. The Input components render this Label through InputLabel. Figma's Info isn't drawn like the Hugeicons one.

## Variants

`labelVariants` (cva):

| Prop | Options | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `default`, `read-only`, `disabled` | `default` |

## Props

Documented props only; every component also accepts the props of the element or Base UI part it renders (`className`, events, ARIA…).

`LabelProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` | The text of the label. |
| `requirement?` | `React.ReactNode` | Text after the label, like "(obrigatório)" or "(opcional)". |
| `info?` | `React.ReactNode` | Shows the Info icon next to the label with this content in a tooltip. |

## Types

`LabelProps`, `LabelState`

## Rules

- Import `Label` from `@lucasdost/design-system`. Do not rebuild it with plain HTML and Tailwind classes.
- Style it through its props and variants first. Use `className` only for layout (margin, width, grid placement), never to change its colors, typography or radius.
- Colors come from the S0L tokens; see [color](../foundations/color.md).
